memo.verdict: Neutral; park at this price; conviction medium. DiscoverIE (DSCV-GB) at 895.0p (2026-10-12) is a cyclical demand recovery inside a steady acquisitive compounder whose recovery has already been priced: the operating change is real and sector-confirmed, adjusted EPS compounds about 10 percent a year on the record's modal path, and the modal total shareholder return is 8.2 percent a year over eighteen months and 8.6 percent a year over three years against the framework's 20 percent bar. The park rule's gates are not tripped (management B, business quality C, predictability B, trackability C); the case is parked on the return, which the price has taken. Progress to Early-Stage only if the shares fall to about 765p or below (where the eighteen-month modal path clears 20 percent a year), or if the half-year results (1 December 2026 on the earnings review's date; 2026-12-08 on the financials block's) show organic revenue growth of 7 percent or more with book-to-bill at or above 1.1 times and gearing at or below 2.0 times; even then the eighteen-month return at 895.0p is about 9.4 percent a year, so the price trigger binds, not the evidence trigger.
case: - The change is external and cyclical, and it is real. An 18-month customer destocking cycle has ended: organic orders rose 31 percent year on year in the three months to 30 June 2026 from 15 percent the quarter before; organic revenue rose 6 percent from 5 percent; book-to-bill was 1.15 times; the last laggard unit, Controls (six large North American customers whose destocking took twice as long as expected), returned to organic growth in Q4 FY26. The orders are non-cancellable and over 90 percent fall due within twelve months (about four months near-term, six to twelve months longer-dated), so the next two halves of revenue are largely written. The turn is sector-wide: book-to-bill above 1.1 times across several European connectivity makers with distribution channels destocked (AlphaSense's view of 10 October 2026, unchecked), and the European manufacturing PMI at 52.7 in August 2026, the highest since May 2022. Design wins, which restocking does not produce, rose 8 percent to about £385m of lifetime value in FY26.

- The company's own cycle has turned with each successive reading higher: organic sales minus 10 percent H1 FY25, minus 7 percent FY25, plus 2 percent FY26, plus 5 percent Q4 FY26, plus 6 percent Q1 FY27; reported half-year revenue growth minus 4.9, minus 1.5, plus 2.5, plus 7.1 percent across H1 FY25 to H2 FY26.

- The change inside the company is continuity under more pressure. The same two executives run the same strategy; what changed is pace and funding: £95m on three deals in six months at an average 9 times EBIT; gearing from 1.2 times to 2.2 times pro forma with a path back to 1.8 times by March 2027; a Bangalore plant with three times the prior Indian capacity opened August 2026; the margin ambition raised to 17 percent by FY30 (June 2025, the tenth upward revision in fifteen years); security added as a fifth target market (September 2024); margin expansion now planned two-thirds from acquisitions and one-third organic against an even split over the past decade. Pricing is real (gross margin up 0.5 points in FY26 to a record and 8.3 points since FY18; annual increases of 3 to 5 percent accepted per one expert; tariff costs passed through at nil margin). Capacity investment adds £4.4m of operating cost in FY26, about a £2m ongoing EBIT drag per Deutsche Bank, with capital spending rising from £6.6m to about £9m in FY27. No decisive internal trigger: no chief-executive change, no numeric guidance.
counter_case: - At Building Block 1, in its strongest form: the 31 percent order surge is safety restocking, not demand. Customers are lengthening their order horizons "to secure supply safety" as supplier delivery times lengthen, the company's own description and the PMI's lengthening-delivery-times reading, and that is exactly how the 2021 to 2022 inventory build began before the 2024 to 2025 destock. The comparison base was the weakest quarter of the cycle. The continental European industrial base is flat: German industrial production fell 1.6 percent month on month in July 2026, machinery output is forecast flat for 2026, France is weaker still, and the company's correlation with the composite PMI is 0.8. When the restock passes, organic growth settles at 2 to 4 percent; the margin path then depends entirely on deals bought at rising multiples (9 times on the last three, 11 to 12 times EBITA for 3Gmetalworx) with money at 5 to 6 percent, so EPS compounds 5 to 7 percent a year; and the market, which paid about 14 times for this business for most of 2024 and 2025, goes back there. At 14.0 times on 52p of 24-month-forward earnings the shares are worth about 730p plus dividends by April 2028, a loss of about 16 percent. This is the Risks report's "false friend" path of June 2026 with the flattering indicator now being orders rather than cash conversion, and the environment is its friend: Fragility at Double Underweight, European breadth at three-year lows, a market that pays for existing cash and refuses leverage. The evidence: the weak comparative; the longer-dated orders; the German data; restock warnings from both covering brokers on 24 July 2026; Volex's medical segment still shrinking 10.5 percent organically on destocking; 2.2 times gearing that pauses the deal engine for a year. The combination that would make it fatal is the 'Pret sandwich' the Risks report built: organic growth of 5 percent a year, margin expansion two-thirds dependent on deals, deals funded at 5 to 6 percent with gearing at 2.2 times, unhedged translation on 79 percent of revenue, flat engineering headcount, a 33-year dual tenure with thin succession, and a multiple at the two-year 99th percentile; together, in a European industrial stall with a strong pound, adjusted EPS of about 35p and a fair value near 470p.

- The record's response. Conceded: part of the 31 percent is restocking; the durable branch carries only 45 percent and the multiple de-rates in the blend for that reason; the comparatives will take reported order growth down sharply in the second half whatever underlying demand does; the deal engine is paused by leverage until mid-2027. Held on the operating view: the orders are non-cancellable and the business does not accept cancellations, so the restock, if that is what it is, is already revenue for the next two halves; the turn is visible across the sector and in distribution, not only in this company; design wins, which are not restocking, rose 8 percent; Controls' problem was customer-specific inventory, now cleared; the cost base is variable, so a shallower recovery costs growth, not margin; the company has never, in the record before us, turned an order surge into a profit warning. Not held on the investment view at this price: the competing hypothesis does not need to be right for the shares to disappoint; it needs only to be plausible enough to cost two or three points of multiple, and at 18.5 times and the 99th percentile of two years it is. It is the reason the modal multiple is 16.9 times rather than 18.5 and the reason the recommendation is neutral and parked rather than bullish.
triggers: - Price trigger: progress to Early-Stage at about 765p or below (766p on the eighteen-month modal path; 663p on the three-year path; 837p on the multiple-held branch alone); 'OSHQC CfC Clearing' would re-fit at about 695p or below with the operating evidence intact.

- Evidence trigger: the half-year results (1 December 2026 or 2026-12-08) at organic revenue growth of 7 percent or more, book-to-bill at or above 1.1 times and gearing at or below 2.0 times move the durable branch to probable (about 60 percent) and the blended multiple to about 17.2 times; the eighteen-month return at 895.0p is still about 9.4 percent a year, so the price trigger binds.

- The durable-turn condition: organic revenue growth of 5 percent or more over the twelve months to September 2027; below 4 percent or book-to-bill below 1.0 moves it to unlikely (about 25 percent) and starts the market-catch-up red flag forming.

- Monitoring levels (Alarm; Invalidate): organic order growth below 5 percent; negative. Book-to-bill 1.00 times; 0.95 times. Organic revenue growth 3 percent; below 2 percent with book-to-bill under 1.00 times. Adjusted operating margin 13.5 percent; below 13.0 percent (a first-half FY27 margin below 13.5 percent at constant currency changes the margin view). Gearing 2.5 times; 3.0 times (gearing above 2.0 times at March 2027 changes the deal-engine view). A deal above 12 times EBIT is an Alarm. The 24-month-forward multiple at 14.4 times on unchanged earnings is an Alarm. A sell-side EPS cut of 2 percent or more is an Alarm on the consensus driver. Modal cases: organic order growth 10 to 15 percent for H1 FY27; book-to-bill 1.05 to 1.10 times; organic revenue growth 5 to 6 percent FY27 and 4 to 5 percent FY28; margin 14.3, 14.7, 15.0 percent FY27 to FY29; gearing 1.8 times by 31 March 2027; deals of about £40m a year from FY29; multiple 16.9 times at both horizons.
- Environment markers that would change the multiple view: a 200-day European breadth reading back above 58 percent with the French spread under 100 basis points, alongside the durable turn.

- Open diligence item for any later stage: the single-source claim (a former Variohm director, 14 November 2025) that about half the sales mix is commoditised and engineering headcount is flat; no rating moved on it.
